newsitem.title: UK: British minister hints at May 1 election.
newsitem.headline: British minister hints at May 1 election.

text.p: A senior member of the British government dropped another broad hint on Saturday that general elections will take place on May 1.
Prime Minister John Major has left the nation guessing for months over his preferred polling day.

The election must take place by May 22, marking the end of the current five-year parliament, but Major has said it will in fact take place no later than May 1 -- the date of county council elections in England.
Speaking to the ruling Conservative Party's local government conference, Education Secretary Gillian Shephard further fuelled speculation that Major has in fact pencilled in a May 1 election.
"On May 1, many of you will be fighting for local government seats and victory. Who knows? Perhaps we shall even be fighting both elections on the same day," she said.

Shephard launched a fierce attack on the education policies of the main opposition Labour Party, accusing it of "con-tricks" and warning that if it won power it would abolish grammar schools, which select pupils according to their ability.
